messages:
Tony: Heads-up — started seeing a burst of ECC/Xid alerts in us-west2 around 12:02 UTC, looks concentrated in rack-r12 (nodes r12n1..r12n4). Alert flood from `dcgm-exporter` — 40+ xid events in 3m.
Maya: ugh, I see the same in dashboards, latency for some dedicated pools spiking as jobs get retried.
Sam: link to alert: https://alerts.internal/redwood/alerts/AC-4821 — dcgm_exporter_xid_count{device="GPU-3",node="r12n2"} > 0 (firing)
dcgm-bot: [alert] dcgm_exporter_xid_count on r12n2 (GPU-3) x42 in 180s — severity: warning. See /alerts/AC-4821
Tony: quick triage idea: sounds like a short-lived burst affecting multiple cards in same rack. Before we drain, can we tweak PromRule suppression to avoid mass noise and only trigger node quarantine if multiple cards show persistent xid > threshold?
Jen (sre): Agreed. Current prom rule is too chatty: `for: 1m` and counts any xid>0. We should try: longer window + grouping + a simple circuit-breaker.
Elaine: Proposed rule (sketch):
```yaml
- alert: GPU_Xid_Node_Wide
  expr: sum by(node)(increase(dcgm_exporter_xid_count[5m])) >= 5
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Node {{ $labels.node }} has >=5 xid events across cards in 5m"
```
Maya: nice. That groups by node; reduces flapping from single-card blips. Also we should add a per-card suppression for ephemeral spikes: only alert per-card if increase(...) >= 3 in 5m.
Sam: Another idea: add a `card_quarantine` synthetic gauge that sets node state when two conditions met: (1) node-wide xid sum >=5 in 5m AND (2) at least 2 cards with increase(...) >=3 in 5m. Then promo rule can alert on that gauge.
Tony: +1. That lets ops trigger automated partial eviction (circuit-breaker) rather than full rack draining.
Jen (sre): Operational playbook notes: if rule fires, run `gpu-scan` on node, check ECC counters, powercycle affected GPUs, if persistent >3 failures in 24h mark RMA candidate. If node-wide and infra capacity constrained, fallback routing to other AZs.
Elaine: Example suppression tweak for existing rule to keep historical context: `record: node:dcgm:xid_5m_sum` then use `absent_over_time` to detect noise bursts.
Sam: Also recommend tagging alerts with `card_serial` in label for easy correlation with asset DB — reduces manual lookups.
Maya: One more pragmatic change: escalate to page only if `for: 10m` + node_quarantine gauge true. Otherwise log as ticket to infra queue. We were getting paged for 30s bursts last night. :sleepy:
Tony: Capacity note — us-west2 has reserve spare GPUs ~8% right now. If we start quarantining nodes, might impact Dedicated customers. Let's set a soft throttle: do not auto-evict if cluster free capacity < 5% (fail safe).
Jen (sre): Will add throttle to orchestration: `if spare_capacity_pct >= 5 then auto-quarantine else mark for manual triage`.
dcgm-bot: [info] pr opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge/3245 — implements node_quarantine recording rule + updated prometheus rules for 5m windows.
Elaine: I'll run a canary in staging with the new rule for 6 hours, then roll to prod if no missed true-positives.
Sam: If anyone oncall sees more than 3 rack-level incidents in 24h, escalate to infra rotation — could be thermal or PSU related.
Tony: Thanks team. Action items: Elaine deploys rule to staging, Jen wires orchestration throttle, Sam wires card_serial labels, Maya updates playbook with drain/runbook. I'll follow up in #incidents if we need to start manual drains. :thumbsup:
